title: Great Mosque of Agadez
summary: The Grand Mosque of Agadez stands in the historic centre of Agadez, Niger, next to the Sultan's Palace. UNESCO documents say the mosque took its present appearance in the early 16th century, and describe its mudbrick minaret as 27 m high and held to be the tallest ever built entirely of mudbrick.

uncertainty.note: UNESCO's evaluation says the mosque took its general present-day appearance in the early 16th century and the nomination dates the minaret to the 16th century; a partial reconstruction of the minaret followed in the 19th century.

as_recorded.value: took on its general present-day appearance in the early 16th century

where.modern_name: Great Mosque of Agadez, Agadez, Niger
where.historical_name: Grand Mosque of the Sultanate of Aïr, Agadez

importance.justification: Part of the UNESCO-listed Historic Centre of Agadez; its minaret is held to be the tallest mudbrick structure.
